newsitem.title: MALAWI: Migrating teachers seen fuelling spread of AIDS.
newsitem.headline: Migrating teachers seen fuelling spread of AIDS.

text.p: Migrating teachers in search of higher pay in neighbouring countries are fuelling the spread of the deadly AIDS disease and HIV infection in southern African, a Batswana educationalist said on Thursday.

"Every month we are having to repatriate bodies or teachers dying," University of Botswana lecturer Sheila Dinotshe Tlou told a three-day conference of the European Union and Southern African Development Community (SADC) on AIDS and HIV.

She gave no figures but said the problem orginated with the fact that most countries in the region paid their teachers poorly, encouraging them to migrate to neighbouring states with better economies such as Botswana.

"We encourage free movement of our citizens. But is there a time we'll say they should undergo compulsory HIV tests?," Tlou asked, adding the conference should debate whether forced tests would be unfair discrimination.

Nearly 65 percent of the world's sufferers of AIDS, Aquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome, live in Africa which is believed to be the original home of the disease that has contributed to the deaths of six million people around the globe.
SADC's 12 member states are Mauritius, Angola, Lesotho, Swaziland, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Namibia, Mozambique, Tanzania, Malawi, South Africa and Botswana.
